data.title: EU approves teclistamab monotherapy for earlier myeloma use
data.description:
Johnson & Johnson has secured European Commission approval for an indication extension of teclistamab monotherapy for adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior therapy.

The decision broadens access to the bispecific T‑cell engager in the second-line setting and follows the recent approval of teclistamab plus daratumumab.

Many patients relapse after first-line treatment and options narrow once disease becomes refractory to established classes. The company said the new authorisation reinforces the potential of teclistamab across monotherapy and combination approaches at first relapse.

Cyrille Touzeau explained: “Patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma often experience shorter remissions and diminishing responses with each subsequent line of therapy, making effective treatment at first relapse increasingly important.

“The approval of teclistamab monotherapy gives physicians an additional immunotherapy option in the second-line setting, supported by significant improvements in both progression-free and overall survival.”

Ester in ’t Groen said: “Building on the recent approval of teclistamab plus daratumumab, this European Commission further reinforces the strength of bispecific-based immunotherapy approaches as early as second line.

“Together, the MajesTEC-3 and MajesTEC-9 studies support the potential of teclistamab-based therapies to advance the treatment paradigm and improve outcomes for patients earlier in their disease journey.”

Yusri Elsayed added: “Today’s approval marks another important step in our ambition to bring innovative immunotherapies earlier in the treatment journey for patients with multiple myeloma.”

“With positive phase 3 results from both MajesTEC-3 and MajesTEC-9, we continue to build evidence for teclistamab-based regimens across a broad second-line patient population.”

The EC decision is supported by phase 3 data showing teclistamab reduced risk of disease progression or death by 71% and risk of death by 40% compared with standard of care. The updated label introduces a simplified dosing schedule, including monthly dosing from month 7 and earlier transition for eligible patients.

data.title: Sitryx reports phase 1b data for SYX-5219
data.description:
Sitryx Therapeutics has announced positive topline phase 1b results for SYX-5219, a first-in-class oral PKM2 modulator being developed for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.

The findings provide the first clinical evidence that targeting PKM2 to modulate immune cell metabolism can deliver meaningful benefit for patients with atopic dermatitis. SYX-5219 was safe and well tolerated over the six-week treatment period, with pharmacokinetic and target engagement findings consistent with earlier healthy volunteer studies.

Iain Kilty said: “These positive results are an exciting milestone for Sitryx and a testament to the excellent execution by our team and clinical partners.”

He added: “We have provided the first human validation for a differentiated oral therapy, demonstrating activity across multiple clinical endpoints and biomarkers in patients with atopic dermatitis.”

The randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial enrolled 35 adults across sites in the United States and Europe. Patients received SYX-5219 or placebo for six weeks, followed by a 14-day off-treatment period. Differences from placebo were observed from Day 8, increasing throughout the dosing period. SYX-5219 met exploratory efficacy targets for skin disease severity, measured by EASI, and itch, measured by PP-NRS.

At six weeks, the placebo-adjusted change in total EASI score was approximately 28%, while the placebo-adjusted difference in PP-NRS itch score was around 48%. An increasing number of patients achieved at least a one-point improvement in vIGA, supported by reductions in several atopic dermatitis biomarkers.

Biomarker decreases included CCL-17/TARC and CCL-11/eotaxin, which significantly correlated with improvements in disease activity. Additional exploratory findings, including reductions in IL-13 and IgE, support investigation of PKM2 modulation in asthma and other inflammatory diseases.

data.title: Hansa reports positive PAES results for Idefirix at ASN Kidney Week
data.description:
Hansa Biopharma has announced positive data from the European Post‑Authorization Efficacy and Safety study of Idefirix, presented in the High‑Impact Clinical Trials session at ASN Kidney Week 2026. The open‑label trial evaluated 50 crossmatch‑positive deceased‑donor kidney transplants across Europe and was selected as a late‑breaking abstract at the congress.

Renée Aguiar‑Lucander, CEO of Hansa Biopharma, said: “The presentation of the PAES study in the High-Impact Clinical Trials session highlights the scientific and clinical relevance of these findings and the potential of imlifidase to address a significant unmet need for highly sensitized patients awaiting kidney transplantation. We are encouraged by the continued interest from the transplant community in the growing body of evidence supporting imlifidase.”

The study reported a one‑year graft failure‑free survival rate of 90% at 12 months post‑transplant. Graft survival reached 92% and patient survival 98%, with Idefirix generally well tolerated and showing a safety profile consistent with previous clinical experience.

Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d’Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, and investigator for the trial, said: “The successful completion of the PAES study provides important evidence in a patient population that continues to face significant challenges in accessing kidney transplantation.

“These findings add to the clinical evidence supporting the use of imlifidase to enable transplantation in highly sensitized patients with a positive crossmatch against a deceased donor.”

ASN Kidney Week is one of the leading global scientific meetings in nephrology and transplantation, with the High‑Impact Clinical Trials session reserved for studies considered among the most clinically relevant at the congress. The abstract was presented by Dr Bestard on behalf of the PAES investigators.

data.title: Mad for it
data.description:
MAD World Summit 2026 has secured official accreditation from The CPD Group, strengthening its position as a must-attend event for professionals looking to transform workplace health, wellbeing and culture.

Taking place on 26 November at Convene, 155 Bishopsgate, London, the summit will bring together senior leaders and industry experts to explore how organisations can turn employee wellbeing into a tangible business advantage.

The accreditation offers attendees three key benefits:

  • Collect CPD Credits: Earn trackable CPD credits to support annual professional development requirements.
  • Receive a Personalised Certificate: Obtain a complimentary certificate of attendance recognising your commitment to ongoing learning.
  • Access High-Quality Content: Gain valuable insights into workplace mental health and wellbeing through expert-led presentations, discussions and interactive sessions.
  •  

With representatives from organisations including BAE Systems, BNP Paribas, Wellcome Trust, Serco, EDF, Dentons LLP, Aston University and National Highways, the summit will provide a valuable platform for cross-sector collaboration, fresh perspectives and actionable strategies.

For more information, visit: https://madworldsummit.com/cpd-accreditation/

View the live agenda here: https://madworldsummit.com/mad-world-agenda-2026/

Book your MAD World Summit 2026 pass here: https://madworldsummit.com/delegate-pass/

data.title: Hutchmed reports phase 3 SANOVO data for first‑line lung cancer
data.description:
Hutchmed has announced positive phase 3 results from the SANOVO trial evaluating ORPATHYS plus TAGRISSO in treatment‑naïve patients with EGFR‑mutated non‑small cell lung cancer and MET overexpression. The data, presented at ESMO Congress 2026, showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in progression‑free survival compared with TAGRISSO alone.

Professor Yi‑Long Wu said: “The SANOVO results mark a pivotal evolution in how we approach first-line EGFR-mutated lung cancer. Historically, co-occurring MET alterations have been associated with poor outcomes on EGFR-TKI treatment, increasing the motivation to test for MET alterations at diagnosis and upon progression.

These potentially practice-changing results showed that adding savolitinib to osimertinib extended median PFS by more than a year in the high MET population, and 11 months overall, in first-line MET-overexpressing EGFR-mutated lung cancer.

“Coupled with highly encouraging clinical benefit in OS, these data reinforce the transformative potential of this all-oral, biomarker-directed treatment approach for a patient population where co-occurring MET overexpression may limit the long-term benefits of EGFR-TKI monotherapy.”

In the intention‑to‑treat population, the combination reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 44%, with median PFS reaching 24.9 months versus 13.8 months for TAGRISSO alone. In the high MET subgroup, risk reduction reached 55%, with median PFS of 24.8 months compared with 11.1 months. Overall survival also improved, with median OS of 44.5 months versus 34.9 months and three‑year survival rates of 67.4% versus 47.4%.

Mr Johnny Cheng, Acting Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer of Hutchmed, said: “SANOVO, alongside the SAFFRON and SACHI studies, establishes a comprehensive treatment continuum for the ORPATHYS plus TAGRISSO combination – spanning frontline intervention to post-EGFR-TKI resistance.

“SANOVO demonstrates that by identifying MET overexpression at diagnosis and initiating an all oral, dual-targeted combination upfront, we can meaningfully extend PFS and OS while preserving patient quality of life.”

data.title: Microbiotica presents phase 1b data for MB097 at ESMO 2026
data.description:
Microbiotica has presented new phase 1b clinical data for MB097, its oral precision microbiome therapeutic for advanced melanoma, at the ESMO Congress 2026 in Madrid. The MELODY‑1 trial met all primary and secondary endpoints and showed encouraging efficacy signals in a population refractory to anti‑PD‑1 therapy.

Professor Paolo Ascierto said: “The advanced melanoma patients enrolled in MELODY‑1 had recently received anti-PD-1 therapy but continued to experience disease progression. Many had received multiple prior lines of treatment, including combination immune checkpoint inhibitor regimens, without achieving a meaningful clinical benefit.

“This represents a particularly challenging patient population with limited therapeutic options. It is therefore encouraging to observe clinically meaningful responses, including deep tumour regressions, suggesting that modulation of the gut microbiome with MB097 may help restore sensitivity to pembrolizumab in patients previously refractory to anti-PD-1 therapy.

He added: “These findings provide an important early clinical proof-of-concept for microbiome-based strategies aimed at enhancing the effectiveness of cancer immunotherapy and warrant further investigation in larger clinical studies.”

The poster presentation highlighted that MB097 was safe and well tolerated in combination with pembrolizumab, with no serious adverse effects related to MB097. The nine‑strain consortium showed rapid and persistent engraftment, particularly in patients receiving vancomycin preconditioning. Three of 21 patients in the vancomycin arm achieved an objective response, including one complete response, compared with two of 20 in the non‑vancomycin arm.

The international study enrolled 41 patients whose melanoma had failed to respond at any time to anti‑PD‑1 therapy. Participants were randomised to receive either five days of vancomycin followed by washout or no preconditioning before starting MB097 plus pembrolizumab for 24 weeks. All patients completed treatment and safety follow‑up.

Robert Tansley, Chief Medical Officer of Microbiotica, said: “Growing evidence highlights the role of the gut microbiome in patients’ responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors, particularly anti-PD-1 therapies.

“The data presented at ESMO from our phase 1b MELODY-1 study demonstrates that MB097 was safe and well tolerated in combination with KEYTRUDA, with robust, persistent engraftment of the bacterial consortium and encouraging clinical responses in this challenging patient population.”

data.title: Radiotherapy boosts progression‑free survival in advanced lung cancer
data.description:
Patients with oligometastatic non‑small cell lung cancer lived significantly longer without disease progression when radiotherapy was added to standard systemic therapy, according to new phase 2 data presented at the ESMO Congress 2026. The SARON trial, funded by Cancer Research UK and sponsored by UCL, found progression‑free survival increased from 8.9 to 13.9 months – a 56% improvement.

Dr Fiona McDonald, Consultant Thoracic Clinical Oncologist at The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust and Leader of the Thoracic Radiotherapy Group at The Institute of Cancer Research, London, who is Chief Investigator of the SARON trial, said: “Until now, there has been limited randomised evidence about the benefits of adding radiotherapy to the standard of care systemic treatment for patients with oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The SARON trial has provided important data in this context, demonstrating a significant improvement in progression-free survival without compromising quality of life.

The trial enrolled 140 patients across 19 UK centres, all with between one and five metastases in three or fewer organs. Participants were randomised to receive either standard systemic therapy alone or systemic therapy plus local consolidation radiotherapy delivered to all known disease sites. High‑dose radiotherapy included stereotactic ablative radiotherapy where appropriate.

After a median follow‑up of 37.4 months, only 13% of patients receiving radiotherapy experienced progression at initial disease sites within 12 months, compared with 39.5% in the standard‑treatment arm. Overall survival was similar between groups, at 31 months versus 28 months respectively, and radiotherapy was well tolerated without significant impact on quality of life.

Julie Moran, a 69‑year‑old former Senior Cardiac Technician from Buckinghamshire, was diagnosed with oligometastatic lung cancer after long COVID symptoms led to further investigation. She said: “In a way, COVID saved my life. Without it, my symptoms might have gone under the radar.

“It’s strange to be diagnosed with lung cancer after working in heart and lung care for so long, because you can really see it from the patient’s perspective. Even after seeing so many ECG scans throughout my career, when I saw my own one, it was off the scale.”

data.title: ViiV and Axmed expand access to HIV medicines
data.description:
ViiV Healthcare has signed an agreement appointing Axmed as a non-exclusive distributor to support procurement and supply of its HIV medicines in more than 50 middle-income countries, subject to local regulatory requirements.

The partnership aims to provide a simpler route to access more choice in HIV care and strengthen national HIV responses. Most new HIV cases occur in low- and middle-income countries, where access challenges remain significant.

Axmed operates a technology-enabled business-to-business platform connecting healthcare procurers with suppliers to improve access to medicines. Through its digital tools, governments and healthcare institutions can lower procurement costs and streamline logistics, helping health systems reach more people with available resources. Middle-income countries often face distinct barriers and may not qualify for certain lower-income access mechanisms, underscoring the need for new models to expand access.

Deborah Waterhouse said: “This agreement underlines ViiV Healthcare’s leadership in the global HIV response and our deep understanding of the realities in middle-income countries.”

She added: “Shaped by listening closely to communities and governments, this announcement is an important step in supporting them to access more choice in HIV care, strengthen health systems and accelerate progress towards our shared goal of ending the HIV epidemic.”

Emmanuel Akpakwu said: “The promise of medical innovation is only fulfilled when it reaches the people who need it. Technology gives us an extraordinary opportunity to reimagine how that happens, connecting fragmented markets, unlocking more affordable procurement and streamlining access to vital medicines.”

He added: “Through this agreement with ViiV Healthcare, we are working towards a future where more people can benefit from advances in HIV care, regardless of where they live.”

Both organisations share a commitment to improving access in countries where health systems face challenges. As the number of people living with HIV continues to rise, the agreement supports ViiV Healthcare’s ambition to broaden access through partnerships, programmes and technologies.

data.title: FDA approves Hibsago for chronic hepatitis B
data.description:
The FDA has approved GSK’s Hibsago for adults with chronic hepatitis B virus infection who meet specific virological criteria and have been receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy for at least six months. The antisense oligonucleotide is the first treatment to show functional cure rates far exceeding the current standard of care.

Tony Wood said: “Despite current therapies, many people living with chronic hepatitis B remain on treatment indefinitely and continue to face the risk of serious liver complications.

“For the first time, with Hibsago, US patients have the potential to achieve functional cure after a six-month treatment course, with the added convenience of the option of self-administration after the first dose.”

The approval is based on phase 3 B‑Well trials, which showed functional cure rates of 19% in adults with baseline HBsAg levels ≤3000 IU/ml. Current standard of care typically achieves less than 1% functional cure after one year of treatment. Functional cure is defined as undetectable HBV DNA and HBsAg for at least 24 weeks after stopping all therapy.

Dr Norah Terrault said: “This is the start of a new era in treating people living with CHB. Bepirovirsen offers patients the potential to achieve functional cure after a short period of treatment, a long-standing goal for patients and physicians alike.”

Dr Chari Cohen said: “CHB is a major public health challenge, affecting millions of people in the US and accounting for approximately 56% of all global liver cancer cases.

“Today marks significant progress towards our aim of transforming the way CHB is managed with improvements in screening, diagnosis and the availability of innovative treatment options for our community.”

Quantitative surface antigen testing will support identification of suitable patients, with several FDA‑authorised tests available. GSK is advancing regulatory submissions for bepirovirsen globally, with key decisions expected soon.

data.title: FDA approves Enspryng for at‑home TED treatment
data.description:
The FDA has approved Genentech’s Enspryng for adults with thyroid eye disease, making it the first at‑home subcutaneous treatment option for the condition. The therapy can be administered every four weeks during the maintenance phase by the person living with TED or a caregiver after appropriate training.

Levi Garraway said: “Today’s FDA approval of Enspryng provides an important new option for people with thyroid eye disease, who have long faced limited treatment choices.

“As the first subcutaneous treatment for this condition, Enspryng offers a positive safety and efficacy profile and the potential for at-home administration.”

César A Briceño explained: “Treating thyroid eye disease requires balancing efficacy, safety and the practical realities of long-term treatment.

“As a clinical trial investigator, I have seen firsthand the potential of targeted therapies such as Enspryng. The availability of an effective subcutaneous treatment option could provide greater flexibility for both patients and physicians while reducing the logistical burden associated with infusion-based therapies.”

The approval is based on the phase 3 SatraGO programme. While SatraGO‑1 did not meet its primary endpoint at week 24, SatraGO‑2 showed significant improvements in proptosis response and diplopia reduction in the active TED population. No new safety signals were identified, with the profile consistent with that seen in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.

Christine Gustafson said: “Thyroid eye disease not only affects a person’s eyes through bulging and vision problems, but it also takes a profound emotional toll on confidence, identity, relationships and daily life.

“Until now, our community has had very limited choices. The approval of Enspryng represents a critical turning point through a convenient, targeted option.”

The decision marks the second indication for Enspryng following its approval in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder in 2020. The medicine is also under priority review for myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody‑associated disease and is being studied in additional autoimmune and inflammatory conditions.
